1. **nix/modules/project/settings/all.nix:422** — The actual bug (discussion #430: multiple modules setting `settings.<pkg>.custom` conflict as "defined multiple times") is not fixed by `default = lib.id;`. A default only applies when *no* module sets the option; it does nothing when two or more modules each assign a real function to `custom` (exactly the reported scenario, e.g. haskell-flake's own internal defaults plus a user's `haskellProjects.default.settings.foo.custom`). The module system will still error on conflicting definitions of a `functionTo types.package` option. Request: actually reproduce the discussion #430 scenario and verify it now succeeds; if it doesn't, the merge/priority behavior needs to change (e.g. via `mkOverride`/restructuring how internal defaults are applied), not just adding a default.

2. **nix/modules/project/settings/all.nix:422 (comment)** — The comment "Identity function allows composition without conflicts" is misleading/incorrect given point 1 — a default doesn't enable composition of multiple explicit definitions. Fix or remove the comment so it doesn't misstate what the change does.

3. **Missing regression test** — Unlike the (reverted) devshell fix which added a test, this change has no test demonstrating the discussion #430 scenario (two separate config sources setting `custom` on the same setting name) actually works post-fix. Request a `test/` case that exercises this before merging, since this is exactly what the maintainer is trying to verify.

4. **Scope/PR hygiene** — The PR title/description/branch still describe the original (wrong) `mkShellArgs.packages` devshell fix; the diff now addresses a completely different issue per the maintainer's correction. Title, description, and "Changes"/"Testing" sections should be rewritten to match what's actually being shipped (the `custom` option change), not left describing the superseded devshell work — as-is it's confusing for anyone reading the PR history or changelog.
